chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If a man who is insolvent (poor/debt-ridden) has another man perform Hajj on his behalf, that counts as one Hajj for him. So if he becomes affluent afterwards, the Hajj (obligation) remains upon him. And similarly, the Nasibi (Hostile One) when he recognizes (the Wilayah), the Hajj is upon him, even if he had already performed Hajj.

key_terms.النَّاصِب: The Nasibi (one hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Does a Hajj performed while poor count if one later becomes wealthy, and what is the ruling for the Nasibi?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that Hajj performed by an insolvent person is valid and sufficient for the obligatory duty, with no need for repetition upon acquiring wealth, a ruling derived from the principle that the obligation is lifted once performed. It further extends this logic to the 'Nasibi' (those hostile to the Imams), establishing that their prior Hajj does not exempt them from the new obligation once they recognize the Wilayah, highlighting the Shia view of the spiritual efficacy of the act versus the status of the actor. This distinction underscores the juristic nuance between the validity of the ritual and the persistence of the duty based on changing circumstances.
